meaning: to work or study late into the night
literal_translation: trabajar o estudiar hasta muy tarde en la noche
example: I had to burn the midnight oil to finish my project before the exam.
origin: Comes from the time before electric lights, when people used oil lamps to work or study late at night.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to waste money on things you do not need
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with spending money; it is about working or studying late.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to get up very early in the morning
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom refers to the night, not to early morning hours.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to take a long break from studying
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes working hard late at night, the opposite of resting.

explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' comes from people using oil lamps to keep working or studying late at night. It means to stay up late to work or study, often because of a deadline or an exam.
